info.title: BirdNet-Behavior HTTP API
info.summary: JSON API for a BirdNet-Behavior acoustic monitoring station: open read-only endpoints, plus a small token-authenticated write surface.
info.description:
Everything the dashboard shows is backed by this versioned API under `/api/v2`. Almost every endpoint is a read-only `GET`; the exceptions are the eighteen bearer-token endpoints (ten writes and eight reads whose contents are not public), each marked `bearerAuth` below.

**Authentication.** The read-only endpoints, the WebSocket stream and the health check are intentionally open to anyone who can reach the port — restrict them at the network layer (VPN / reverse-proxy allow-list) if that matters. This is by design, not a bug.

The **bearer-token** endpoints are different: each requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, where the token is the station's `BNB_API_TOKEN`. A station that has not been given one answers `404` on every one of them — the write surface does not exist until an operator enables it, and it is never covered by the `/admin` password's open-when-unset behaviour. Generate a token with `openssl rand -base64 48`; anything shorter than 32 bytes is refused and leaves the write surface off.

**Not described here.** The live audio stream at `/stream`, RSS/iCal feeds under `/feeds/*`, and per-detection public share pages under `/r/{token}` are part of the surface but are not under `/api/v2`; see the project docs. Every route served under `/api/v2` is described, and a test fails when one is added without being added here. The two live WebSockets (`/ws/detections`, `/ws/spectrogram`) are described with the status that upgrades them, `101`; the messages they then carry are in that response.

**Analytics.** The `/analytics/*` and `/timeseries/*` families are powered by the bundled DuckDB engine, which is on by default. When it is disabled (or not compiled in), those endpoints answer `200` with a body of `{"status":"unavailable",...}` rather than failing.

**Base URL.** A `GET` to the API root (`/api/v2`, no trailing slash) returns the API name, version and status.

servers.description: Versioned API root, relative to the station's base URL (default http://localhost:8502).

tags.name: analytics

tags.name: timeseries
tags.description: DuckDB time-series aggregations (trend, diversity, peaks, gaps).

tags.name: export
tags.description: Bulk export of detections and species.

tags.name: settings

tags.name: live
tags.description: Live audio from the station's sources, as HLS. The MP3 stream is `GET /stream`, outside `/api/v2`.

servers.description: The API root is exactly `/api/v2`. A path must begin with `/`, so under the `/api/v2` server it could only be spelled `/`, which is `/api/v2/` and is not routed (404). This path item therefore names its own server.

get.description: The API's name, version and status. Served at `/api/v2` with no trailing slash; `/api/v2/` is a 404.
The machine-readable description of this API (this very document).

Use for monitoring. `status` is `healthy` (HTTP 200) or `degraded` (HTTP 503), so an alert can key on the status code alone.

Without `strict`, only a database that is unreachable or has a recorded failed integrity check is degraded. This is the right answer for a container health check: Docker restarts an unhealthy container, and a station whose detection daemon is down is exactly the one that must stay up to be diagnosed.

With `strict`, a stopped detection daemon is degraded too. Point a pager at this form — otherwise a station that has recorded nothing for months answers 200.

503.description: Station is degraded (database integrity check failed).

parameters.name: strict
parameters.description: Also report 503 when the detection daemon is not running. Accepts an empty value, `1`, `true`, `yes` or `on`.

get.description: The station-health conditions as last evaluated by the notifier — a dead microphone, a full disk, a failing backup, a lost data volume, a boot that lost something — and when it looked. These were push-only; this is the pull. Always 200: `/health` carries the verdict, this carries the reasons. `evaluated_at` is null until the first evaluation.
Total detections, unique species, the latest detection and a confidence distribution.
Disk usage for the volume holding the data directory.

503.description: The disk is critically full (`status: critical`), or `df` could not answer for the data directory (`status: unknown`, with `error`).

get.description:
What the Station Health page draws, as JSON: one entry per source the capture supervisor is actually running, with its lifecycle state, uptime, restart history and rolling 24-hour strip.

This is the discovery half of `POST /control/restart-source`: `label` here is what that endpoint takes as `source_id`, and re-reading this is how a caller sees whether the restart took.

`supervised` is `false`, with an empty list, when no capture supervisor is running in this process — web-only mode or tooling. That is an answer, not an error.

label.description: The supervisor's label — the `audio_sources` row id on a station whose sources are managed from `/admin/audio`. This is what `POST /control/restart-source` takes as `source_id`.

uptime_secs.description: Seconds the current process has been running, when connected.

last_audio_age_secs.description: Seconds since this source last delivered fresh audio, if ever observed.

restart_attempts.description: Consecutive (re)start attempts not yet healthy; `0` when connected.

restarts_last_hour.description: Restarts in the last hour whatever the state now — the number that shows a source which keeps coming back.

uptime_24h.description: Rolling 24 hours, oldest first, one entry per half hour.

published_unix.description: When the supervisor last published this snapshot; `0` if never.

401.description: No `Authorization: Bearer` header, or the token does not match.

404.description: This station has no `BNB_API_TOKEN`, so the gated API does not exist.

get.summary: Scheduled maintenance jobs and their state
get.description:
Every job the maintenance loop schedules, with when it last completed, whether it passed, and whether it is due now.

The list is driven by the job catalogue, **not** by the `maintenance_runs` table. That table holds a row per job that has completed at least once, so a listing built from rows would omit exactly the jobs worth asking about — a station whose backup has never run once would show a short, clean list with the problem absent. A job that has never run appears here with `last_run_unix: null` and `due: true`.

`ok` is tri-state and must not be collapsed. `null` means either “never run” or “this job has no pass/fail to report”; `reports_verdict` separates those from a recorded `false`. A session prune that succeeded and an integrity check that failed both have falsy verdicts and mean opposite things.

`due` is the scheduler's own rule, shared with the loop that runs the jobs rather than re-implemented here. It does not account for the loop's in-process floor, which can only delay a job within one process lifetime, so a job reported as due may already have run since its last recorded completion.

200.description: Every scheduled maintenance job and its current state.

now_unix.description: The clock the `due` flags were computed against.

last_run_unix.description: When it last completed; null if it never has.

next_due_unix.description: When it next falls due; null if it has never run.

ok.description: Its last verdict. Null means never run, or no verdict to report — see `reports_verdict`.

reports_verdict.description: Whether this job records a pass/fail at all. When false, a null `ok` is not a failure.

due.description: Whether it is due to run.

due_reason.description: Why it is due, or null when it is not.

500.description: The job state could not be read. Answered as an error rather than as an empty list, which would read as "nothing is due".

get.summary: The database: engine, tables, write latency and the last day's arrivals
get.description: birdnet-go's database overview for its SQLite engine, with three differences, each to avoid a number nobody measured. `integrity_check` is the last recorded integrity check (`ok`, `failed` or `unchecked`), where upstream always answers `ok`. `wal_checkpoints`, `busy_timeouts` and every performance figure but `write_latency_avg_ms` are null: nothing on this station counts them, and upstream's checkpoint count comes from running a checkpoint, which a GET here does not. Table sizes read every page of the file, so they are measured at most every 15 minutes; `tables_measured_at` says when. A database that cannot be read answers 200 with `status: disconnected` and empty lists.

size_bytes.description: The main file's size; the WAL is `sqlite.wal_size_bytes`.

last_vacuum_at.description: When the backup-and-VACUUM job last ran (RFC 3339, UTC), or null if it never has.

size_bytes.description: Bytes of the table's pages and its indexes'.

tables_measured_at.description: Unix seconds when the table sizes were measured.

write_latency_avg_ms.description: Mean detection write since the process started; null before the first.

detection_rate_24h.description: Detections stored in each UTC hour of the last 24, hours with none left out.

401.description: No bearer token, or the wrong one.

get.description: Every interface with its hardware address, its addresses and prefix lengths, and byte counters since it came up; loopback last. An onboarding aid — the address to type when `.local` names do not resolve.

mac.description: Hardware address; null when the interface has none.

addresses.description: Each address with its prefix length, e.g. `192.168.1.20/24`.

get.description: The station's own process first, then every process it started (capture `ffmpeg` / `arecord`, conversions), with CPU sampled over `sample_ms`. Not the whole machine: the question this answers is which of the station's own processes is busy.

cpu_percent.description: CPU over the sample, as a percentage of one core — two busy cores read 200.

get.description: The band levels of the most recent hour that has any, for one capture source, with the broadband A- and Z-weighted figures beside them and the **unit** they are in. The unit is in the payload because it can be either: an uncalibrated station reports `dBFS` (negative, station-relative, fine for tracking change at one place) and a calibrated one reports `dB SPL`. A station with no observations answers 200 with `source: null`, `bands: []` and a `note`; that is a statement about the microphone, not an error.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Capture source label. Defaults to the source with the newest reading.

200.description: The newest hour's spectrum, or the no-observations marker.

source.description: The capture source; null when there are no observations.

date.description: Local date of the hour reported.

samples.description: Measurements averaged into the hour; 0 for a source with none.

calibration_db.description: The offset applied to reach dB SPL; 0 for an uncalibrated station.

note.description: Present only when there are no observations.

band_hz.description: Centre frequency of the third-octave band.

500.description: The sound-level read failed.

get.description:
The models (classifiers and range filters) this build knows how to install, each with the sha256 it will be checked against.

The catalogue is **compiled in**, not fetched. A fetched catalogue is a remote document that decides which URL a station downloads hundreds of megabytes from and which digest it checks them against; pinning both in the binary makes the checksum a promise this repository makes, verifiable by anyone reading the source.

There is no install endpoint. Installing is a 400 MB download taking hours on the uplink a field station has — a request handler is the wrong place for it, with nowhere to report progress and a retry that would start a second download beside the first. Use `birdnet-behavior --install-model <id>`, which runs in the foreground where failing is visible.

`ships_labels` is false where no labels file accompanies the model; the operator supplies one, and its row count must match the model's output width or species are reported under other species' names.

id.description: Stable id; also the installed filename and a routing target.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex digest the download is verified against. A mismatch is deleted, never installed.

bytes.description: Size, used for the free-space check before downloading.

sample_rate.description: What MODEL_n_SAMPLE_RATE must be set to. Not derivable from the tensor — see G-10 Stage 4.

ships_labels.description: Whether a verified labels file is installed alongside.

use.description: What it is for: a second classifier that can run beside the primary, a classifier that replaces the primary, or a species-occurrence (range) filter for METADATA_MODEL_PATH. For a range filter `sample_rate` is 0.

get.description: Runtime metrics in the Prometheus text exposition format (not JSON).
Detection log, newest first, one page at a time. `date`, `species` and `source` combine: each one given narrows the list. `total_count` is the size of the filtered set.

400.description: Invalid `date` (expected YYYY-MM-DD).

get.description: The last N detections, newest first.
Per-day detection totals over the last `days` days, for trend charts.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: How many days back to include (default 7, clamped to 365).

401.description: No `Authorization: Bearer` header, or the token does not match.

date.description: Local calendar date of the detection, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

sci_name.description: Scientific name exactly as the detection was recorded.

400.description: The key is malformed, or `status` is not a recognised verdict.

post.summary: Apply one operation to many detections
post.description:
One round trip, one authentication and one result document instead of N of each — what a triage client rejecting forty overnight false positives needs.

**This is not a transaction.** Each detection goes through the same code path as the single-detection endpoint, so the SQLite store and the DuckDB analytics copy stay in step; one shared transaction would mean a second implementation of "delete a detection" and is not worth that. A key that matches nothing does not stop the batch either: a client working from a slightly stale list would otherwise have forty good deletions refused because three rows had already gone.

**Read `failed`, not just the status code.** The response is `200` whenever the request itself was well-formed, even if every item failed — the request was understood and carried out, and the per-item outcomes are the body. `applied` and `failed` are at the top level so a caller need not walk `results` to know what happened.

Every detection actually changed is written to the station's audit log individually, under the same action name the single-detection endpoint uses, so "what happened to that recording?" stays answerable. A full batch of 500 writes 500 audit rows, which is one page of the station's audit view.

op.description: Applied to every detection in the list. An unrecognised value is refused rather than ignored.

status.description: `review` only; omit to clear an existing verdict. Sending it with any other `op` is a `400`, because a caller who wrote it believes it did something.

notes.description: `review` only; attached to every verdict in the batch.

detections.description: At most 500 per request; a longer list is refused before anything is written rather than truncated.

date.description: Local calendar date of the detection, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

sci_name.description: Scientific name exactly as the detection was recorded.

com_name.description: Read only when `op` is `review`; defaults to `sci_name`.

200.description: The request was carried out. Check `failed` — this is also the status when every item failed.

failed.description: How many were not — malformed key, no such detection, or a database error.

results.description: One entry per detection, in the order sent.

400.description: An unknown `op`, `status`/`notes` on a non-review `op`, an unparseable verdict, or more than 500 detections.

401.description: No `Authorization: Bearer` header, or the token does not match.

404.description: This station has no `BNB_API_TOKEN`, so the write surface does not exist.

get.description: One row per detection-daemon start, newest first: the SHA-256 of the model and labels it analysed with, the settings in force, and how many detection rows carry it. This is how a season that spans a model swap is split by which model heard what.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Newest `limit` runs; default 50, at most 500.

404.description: No such run.

get.description:
Every persisted setting, with credentials removed two ways: by key name (`email_smtp_pass`, `birdweather_token`) and by value shape, which catches the credential inside a URL such as `ntfy://user:pass@host`. The by-shape rules are blunt: that value comes back as `***@host`, keeping the host and path but not the scheme or username, so a redacted value is not one you can edit and send back. A redacted value is **replaced** with `***REDACTED***` rather than omitted, so a caller can tell a secret it may not read from a setting that was never configured; `redacted` lists exactly which keys those were.

Known gap: a URL whose *path segment* is the credential — a heartbeat ping URL, for instance — is caught by neither rule and is returned in full.

settings.description: Every persisted key, in sorted order.

redacted.description: The keys whose value was replaced with `***REDACTED***`.

401.description: No `Authorization: Bearer` header, or the token does not match.

404.description: This station has no `BNB_API_TOKEN`, so the settings API does not exist.

put.description:
A partial update: send only the keys you mean to change. Values may be strings, numbers or booleans; each is stored as the string the settings table holds, through the same normalisation the admin page uses (so `"51,5"` is stored as `51.5`). A key already holding the value sent is not rewritten and is not counted in `updated`.

Unknown keys are refused rather than ignored — a misspelling that answered 200 would report a change that never happened — and so is the literal `***REDACTED***`, which is what a client gets back from `GET /settings` for a secret and must not write over the real value.

The change is recorded in the station's audit log by key name only, never by value.

schema.description: Setting keys to values. Keys must come from `writable_keys`.

200.description: The settings were written. `updated` is 0 when every value already matched.

400.description: An unknown key, a value with no string form, the `***REDACTED***` placeholder, or a body that is not a JSON object.

401.description: No `Authorization: Bearer` header, or the token does not match.

404.description: This station has no `BNB_API_TOKEN`, so the settings API does not exist.

500.description: The database refused the change.

post.description:
Sends this process `SIGTERM` after a short delay, so the response is written before the socket closes; systemd's `Restart=always` brings a fresh instance up. The request body is ignored.

Answers `503` when the process is not running under systemd, because nothing would then bring the station back — a `200` there would tell the caller the opposite of what is about to happen. The attempt is recorded in the audit log either way.

200.description: `SIGTERM` sent; systemd will start a fresh instance.

401.description: No `Authorization: Bearer` header, or the token does not match.

404.description: This station has no `BNB_API_TOKEN`, so the control API does not exist.

503.description: Not running under systemd, so nothing would restart the process. Nothing was signalled.

post.description:
Stops and restarts a single capture source, leaving every other source recording. On a multi-source station `POST /control/restart` is a blunt instrument: one wedged RTSP camera costs every other microphone its in-flight audio.

The restart goes through the supervisor's own start path, so the recording schedule and the source's quiet window still hold — a source that is `paused` when the request arrives stays paused, and the response says so rather than reporting a restart that will not happen.

`source_id` is the supervisor's label for the source, which is the `audio_sources` row id on any station whose sources are managed from `/admin/audio`. The labels currently supervised are returned with the `404`.

202.description: Request recorded; the supervisor applies it on its next tick.

state.description: The source's last published state. `paused` means the request is spent without a restart.

already_pending.description: A restart was already queued for this source and had not been applied yet.

401.description: No `Authorization: Bearer` header, or the token does not match.

404.description: This station has no `BNB_API_TOKEN`, or no supervised source carries that label.

422.description: The body is not an object with a `source_id` string.

503.description: No capture supervisor is running in this process, so nothing would drain the request.

get.description: Most-detected species with counts and mean confidence.
Case-insensitive search over common and scientific names.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search query (max 200 characters).

400.description: Query too long.

get.description: Summary statistics plus hourly activity for one species.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Common or scientific name of the species.

404.description: No such species.

get.summary: What is notable about a day's species
get.description: For every species detected on the date: first ever, first of the (tracking) year, first of the season, and returning after an absence. The windows the flags are measured against are returned beside the species, because a bare "first this season" is unreadable without knowing which season the station thinks it is in, and that depends on the latitude it was given: a station with no latitude reports `season: null`, and nothing is ever new in a season it does not have. `headline` is the single strongest claim (`first ever`, `returning`, `first this year`, `first this season`), null when nothing is notable.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The day to report, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to today at the station. A value that is not of that shape is ignored and today is used.

parameters.name: notable_only
parameters.description: Return only species with something notable about them.

year_start.description: First date of the tracking year containing `date`.

season.description: The season containing `date`, by the station's latitude; null when it has none.

season_start.description: First date of that season (the year start when the station has no latitude).

absence_days.description: Days of silence after which a detection counts as a return.

days_since_previous.description: Days since the previous detection; null if there was none.

500.description: The tracking read failed.

get.summary: Which species the occurrence filter admits
get.description:
Answers "why is this bird never heard here?" with the number behind it. The station asks a range model which species occur around its location in a given week of the model's 48-week year (four weeks to a month) and admits a species when the model scores it at or above the threshold (`SF_THRESH`), or the operator put it on the Always allowed list, and the operator's include and exclude lists allow it. This lists every species the model scores, most likely first, each with that decision, and `verdict` says which of four ways it came about: `admitted`, `admitted-by-whitelist` (under the threshold, allowed by the list), `held-back-by-range` (under the threshold) or `held-back-by-lists` (over the threshold, kept out by the include or exclude list). `explanation` is the sentence the station's Species page shows. The decision is the filter's own, restated: the species marked admitted are exactly those the detection daemon lets through for that place and week.

The station's coordinates are returned to one decimal place (about 11 km) because the endpoint is as open as the rest of the read API. A station that cannot answer says so with `503` and a `reason`, and no `species` key: an empty list would read as an empty region.

parameters.name: week
parameters.description: The model's week, 1 to 48. Defaults to the current week at the station. Anything else is refused, not clamped: the model reads other values as 'no seasonal information' and answers with a year-round list.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Only species whose common name, scientific name or name in the station's language contains this text (any case).

parameters.name: admitted
parameters.description: `true` for only the species the station admits, `false` for only those it holds back.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Most species to return.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Species to skip, for paging.

200.description: The place, the week, the threshold and the species.

location.description: The station's coordinates, to one decimal place.

week_is_current.description: True when `week` was not asked for and is the current one.

threshold.description: The probability at or above which the model admits a species (`SF_THRESH`).

scored.description: Species the model scores, whatever the selection.

admitted_total.description: Of those, how many the station admits, whatever the selection.

matched.description: How many the selection (`q`, `admitted`) picked, before paging.

common_name.description: The classifier's name, as stored: the key to match on.

display_name.description: `common_name` in the station's language, or itself when it has none.

probability.description: The range model's probability that the species occurs here that week.

explanation.description: One sentence with the real numbers.

400.description: `week`, `admitted`, `limit` or `offset` is not in its range; the message names the range.

503.description: The station cannot say what its occurrence filter does.

error.description: A sentence for a person. Never an empty list: the absence of an answer is not 'nothing occurs here'.

reason.description: `no-location`: the station has no coordinates. `no-range-model`: no range model is loaded, so the filter is off and every species the classifier knows is a candidate. `range-model-failed`: the model is configured and would not run (the station's log has the reason). `no-detection-daemon`: this process is not running the detection daemon.

get.description: Detections per hour (00-23) across all species on a given calendar day.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Calendar day (YYYY-MM-DD).

400.description: Invalid `date`.

get.description: Metadata for a cached Wikipedia/Wikimedia image of the species (URL, attribution, cache status). Fetches and caches on a miss.
The cached image itself. Checks a configured custom image directory first, then the Wikipedia cache.

404.description: No cached image available.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum results (default 50, max 500).

400.description: Invalid filename.

404.description: Recording not found.

400.description: Not a plain file name: path separators and `..` are rejected.

404.description: No detection names this clip.

500.description: The read failed.

get.description: The same selections as an Audacity label track: `begin<TAB>end<TAB>label` per line, the label the common name and the confidence as a percentage. Import it with File, Import, Labels.

400.description: Not a plain file name: path separators and `..` are rejected.

404.description: No detection names this clip.

500.description: The read failed.

get.description: Renders (and caches) a mel spectrogram PNG of a recording. Optional label parameters overlay the species, confidence and time.

parameters.name: species
parameters.description: Overlay species label.

parameters.name: confidence
parameters.description: Overlay confidence (0-100).

parameters.name: time
parameters.description: Overlay time label.

400.description: Invalid filename.

404.description: Recording not found.

422.description: Could not render a spectrogram for this recording.

503.description: Renderer temporarily unavailable (too many concurrent renders).

get.description: Groups consecutive detections of a species into sessions split by an inactivity gap.

parameters.name: gap
parameters.description: Inactivity gap, minutes, that ends a session.

get.description: Ordered window-funnel over a comma-separated species list.

Given a trigger species, the species most often heard immediately after its first detection in an activity session (sessions split at gaps longer than `window` minutes). A species heard in the same audio chunk as the trigger is simultaneous, not next, and is not counted. The trigger can be its own follower (the same bird calling again).

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Trigger species, by common name.

get.description: Given a trigger species, the species most often heard immediately before its first detection in an activity session (sessions split at gaps longer than `window` minutes). A session the trigger opens has no predecessor and is not counted; a species heard in the same audio chunk as the trigger is simultaneous, not previous.

get.description: Whether the DuckDB analytics engine is compiled in and configured. Always available.

Detections per hour of listening, per species per ISO week. A raw count has no denominator: a solar recording window is six hours longer in June than in December, a week of downtime removes a week of listening, a failed microphone halves the channels. This divides the detections made on days with recorded effort by the station time recorded on those days. `effort_hours` is returned beside `detections_per_hour` so a week with little or no listening is visible as such. A day's station time is its longest single source, not the sum across sources, so a two-microphone station is not read as half a one-microphone station. Species-weeks with fewer than `min_detections` detections are left out. Needs the analytics store (DuckDB); it reads `detections_ts` and `recording_effort`, not the behavioural extension. In a build without the analytics engine the body is `{"status":"unavailable", ...}` with HTTP 200 instead.

get.summary: Species phenology: first and last detection per year

A calendar-year window is not a migration window for a resident or an overwintering species. Rows are ordered by year, newest first, then species. The full detection history as CSV (default) or JSON. Rows come from the analytic view: a detection a reviewer rejected, or an imported one on a station that excludes imports from its analytics, is not exported. `Date`/`Time` are the station's local wall clock with no offset; every row also carries `Event_Date` (that wall clock with the offset that was in force, RFC 3339 — in the CSV a column, in JSON `event_date`) and `Detected_At_UTC` (the instant; JSON `detected_at_utc`, epoch seconds), both empty on a row that names no point in time. Every row carries the run that made it: `run_id`, and in the CSV three trailing columns `Run_Id,Model_Name,Model_SHA256`, or in JSON `model_name` and `model_sha256` beside the row — the model file's name and the SHA-256 of its bytes, resolved through `/analysis-runs`. Empty on a row no run of this station produced.

503.description: Every connection slot of this kind is taken; close a tab and retry.

bearerAuth.description: The station's `BNB_API_TOKEN`, resolved from its configuration file and then its environment. Required by every write endpoint, and by the settings read — a station's configuration is not public even with its credentials taken out. The read-only detection, species and analytics endpoints accept no credential and ignore one if it is sent.

Species.name: species
Species.description: Filter to one species (common or scientific name).

Source.name: source
Source.description: Filter to one audio source, by the label detections carry (the `source` field). Combines with every other filter.

Days.name: days
Days.description: How many days back to include.

Weeks.name: weeks
Weeks.description: How many weeks back to include.

Window.name: window
Window.description: Window size (minutes or samples, per endpoint).

MaxGap.name: max_gap
MaxGap.description: Maximum gap, minutes, between steps in a sequence.

HourStart.name: hour_start
HourStart.description: Restrict to detections at or after this hour (0-23).

HourEnd.name: hour_end
HourEnd.description: Restrict to detections before this hour (0-23).

Filename.name: filename
Filename.description: Recording filename (basename only; no path separators or `..`).

AnalyticsResult.description: Analytics result. The exact shape depends on the endpoint; each carries a top-level array of rows plus a `total` count. When the analytics engine is disabled the body is `{"status":"unavailable"}` instead.

schema.description: Endpoint-specific result rows plus counts, or an unavailability marker.

detection_silence_secs.description: Seconds since the most recent stored detection, or null before the first measurement.

analysis_queue_depth.description: Raw segments waiting for analysis after the daemon's last sweep, or null before it reports. Above the shed threshold the daemon analyses one segment in two and raises the `backlog` condition.

detection_deadman.description: The detection deadman's verdict: `tripped` while it has an open quiet episode (no detections for longer than its threshold, or never), a strict fault; `off` when its threshold is 0.

classifiers.description: Each loaded classifier, primary first; empty until the daemon has analysed a file. A failing classifier is degraded under `?strict=1` and raises the `classifier:<id>` condition.

state.description: `failing` once `failure_threshold` windows in a row have failed and none answered since.

windows.description: Analysis windows run since the classifier was loaded.

last_window_at.description: Unix seconds of the latest window, or null before the first.

last_success_at.description: Unix seconds of the latest window answered cleanly, or null for never.

error_class.description: Why the latest failed window failed; null after a clean one.

strict.description: Which mode this response answered in.

detection_writes.description: Whether per-detection writes are currently accepted; `halted` once the daily integrity check has found the database corrupt.

data_volume.description: The data volume's last probe (once a minute): whether a test write succeeded, whether the directory is still its own mount, and the `df` verdict. The string `unchecked` before the first probe. `writable: false` or `mount: vanished` is degraded on every reading; `disk: critical` or `unknown` only under `?strict=1`.

admin_bootstrap.description: Whether the admin-password bootstrap at start succeeded; `failed` is a strict fault.

boot_anomalies.description: What the boot journal found changed since the last start; non-empty is a strict fault.

evaluated_at.description: Seconds since the Unix epoch at which the conditions were evaluated; null before the first evaluation.

body.description: What is wrong and what to do about it.

EngineStatus.description: Availability of an optional engine, plus the endpoints it serves.

DetectionRow.description: One detection. `date`/`time` are the station's local wall clock with no offset, as BirdNET-Pi wrote them; `detected_at_utc` is the instant. Optional fields are omitted when unknown (historical / imported rows).

duration_secs.description: Length of the saved clip in seconds.

run_id.description: The analysis run (`/analysis-runs/{id}`) that produced this row: which model bytes, labels and settings. Absent on a row this station did not analyse — imported history, or rows older than the run table.

detected_at_utc.description: The instant, seconds since the Unix epoch. Absent on a row that names no point in time: a local time that never happened, or an unparseable date.

total_count.description: Rows matching the filters, all pages together (`GET /detections`).

AnalysisRun.description: One detection-daemon start: the model it analysed with, as the SHA-256 of its files, and the run-wide settings. A detection row's `run_id` points here.

model_name.description: The model file's stem: its operator-facing name, not its identity.

model_sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the model file's bytes — the identity.

label_count.description: How many labels the file parsed to — the model's output width.

geomodel_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the occurrence-filter model when one was configured; it decides which species are candidates at all.

detections.description: Detection rows that carry this run.
